inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Three stages: wavy naked DNA lines approaching a recipient cell (oval, containing the circular recipient DNA chromosome); degraded uncombined DNA fragments discarded; the transformed cell containing recipient DNA plus recombined donor DNA.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: Genetics — the conjugation F+ × F− diagram
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: A multi-stage strip: the F+ cell (small circular F plasmid carrying sex-pilus/conjugation genes) building a sex pilus conjugal bridge ('mating bridge') to the F− cell; a single strand of plasmid DNA transferred; both cells ending F+; labeled 'no transfer of chromosomal DNA'.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The F+ plasmid incorporated into the bacterial chromosome (high-frequency recombination cell); transfer of the leading portion of the plasmid along with flanking bacterial chromosome through the bridge; the recipient as a recombinant F− cell (bacterial DNA + bacterial DNA + plasmid copy annotations).

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: A lytic-cycle strip: lytic phage infecting a bacterium; cleavage of bacterial DNA; bacterial DNA packaged in phage capsids; release of new phage from the lysed cell; infecting other bacteria; genes transferred to new bacteria.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: A lysogenic-cycle strip: lysogenic phage infecting a bacterium with viral DNA incorporating into bacterial DNA; the excision event taking flanking bacterial genes; phage particles carrying bacterial DNA; genes different from donor and recipient; the ABCD'S toxin roster printed with it.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: A plasmid containing a transposon; the bacterial DNA chromosome with a marked target site; the transposon copying and excising itself and inserting at the target site; 'integration of genes' as the result.

notes: Census: six printed genetics diagrams (p150: transformation, conjugation F+×F−, Hfr×F−, generalized + specialized transduction; p151: transposition) — raster color-plate art, all COPYRIGHTED; all six redrawn within ONE original KYP registry visual (gene-transfer-triangle, four lanes: transformation / conjugation pair / transduction pair + the transposition card + the route-rules card). The verbatim route text is the note's table block. No FA mnemonics printed on these pages.
